rationale: Both Baroni menus allowed potatoes and gave inconclusive ordinal OFF distributions. The Dresden study measured cold potato salad intake during medicated ON visits. Lunch reduced levodopa concentration variability during infusion without an identified potato exposure or daily OFF endpoint. The direction for roasted potato and daily OFF time remains unresolved.

In the Parkinson trial, some participants receiving corn oil improved on the Hamilton scale and the overall comparison favored DHA plus EPA. The original table, corn oil dose and processing grade remain open. A separate coronary trial using a corn and soybean mixture found inconclusive contrasts against omega-3. None provides an oil-free comparison that isolates refined corn oil.

The existing case involved celery root extract with concurrent medications. Secondary accounts describe hallucinations, and their modality and frequency remain unverified in the original. A pharmaceutical butylphthalide trial reports other adverse events without a visual hallucination frequency measure. Neither exposure identifies a direction for dried celery leaf in Parkinson disease.
